question: To allow for a faster and more flexible response to ‘dynamic border situations’, Frontex has conceived a unit called the Quick Reaction Force (QRF), divided into two sections: a mobile European QRF (E-QRF) with 40 standing corps officers for pan-European support and a contingent QRF (C-QRF) consisting of teams of volunteers under the existing quotas available for ‘emergency situations’.
The QRF staff will not have any periods of inactivity; when not deployed, they will be tasked with training the standing reserve or assigned to ongoing operations. 1.
What details can Frontex provide about the design or launch of the QRF, and what is the timetable for the various steps to be carried out?
What examples can it give of ‘dynamic border situations’ for which the QRF could be deployed?
Where will the QRF be based and to what extent would it also cooperate with the Member States’ special ATLAS units, which are now coordinated by Europol?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.10.2025) As the question falls under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide a response to the question raised by the Honourable Member. The Commission will send the Agency’s reply to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
